result.question: I need to know whether the fault in Transformer 1 at MAIN is getting worse or changing character. Run a DGA fault classification on the first and the last complete oil sample between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Tell me each sample's fault class and confidence. Then tell me whether the class moved toward a higher-energy or higher-temperature fault, for example PD to D1, or T1 to T2/T3. If the two classifications disagree, explain which one you trust more and why, based on the absolute gas levels and not just the ratios. Then recommend one specific next check, such as a confirmatory resample, an OLTC compartment sample or an electrical test. Count a sample as complete only if all five gases are non-null. If there is only one complete sample in the window, classify that one alone and say that no progression can be judged.

**Rogers Ratio (IEC 60599) DGA classification — Transformer 1, MAIN**

(Note: the interpret_dga service was unavailable, so I computed the Rogers ratios manually from the raw gas data.)

**First complete sample — 2024-01-15** (all five gases non-null)
- H₂ = 2845, CH₄ = 7406, C₂H₆ = 5467, C₂H₄ = 16684, C₂H₂ = 7 ppm
- r1 = CH₄/H₂ = 2.60 → code 2; r2 = C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = 0.0004 → code 0; r3 = C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = 3.05 → code 2
- IEC code **0-2-2 → Thermal fault T3 (hot spot > 700 °C)**, confidence: high (r2 decisively < 0.1, r1 and r3 clearly in the >1 and >3 bands — no ratio is near a boundary)

**Last complete sample — 2024-01-18** (all five gases non-null)
- H₂ = 2900, CH₄ = 7350, C₂H₆ = 5450, C₂H₄ = 16600, C₂H₂ = 7 ppm
- r1 = 2.53 → 2; r2 = 0.0004 → 0; r3 = 3.05 → 2
- IEC code **0-2-2 → Thermal fault T3 (> 700 °C)**, confidence: high (identical code, same clear-cut ratios)

**Progression:**
The fault class has **not changed** — both samples classify as T3 (high-temperature thermal fault, > 700 °C), not a lower-energy PD/D1/D2 or T1/T2 class. So there is no movement toward a higher-energy fault; the character is stable. Absolute levels are also essentially flat day over day (ethylene 16,684 → 16,600; hydrogen +55 ppm; acetylene 7 → 7), i.e., no clear worsening within this window — but the fault is severe in absolute terms (ethylene ~16,700 ppm is far above typical T3 thresholds), so this is an ongoing, serious thermal condition rather than an improving one. The classifications do not disagree, so no tie-break judgment is needed.

**Recommended next check:**
Take an **OLTC compartment oil sample** (separate from the main tank) to rule out contaminating migration of switching gases into the main-tank oil — a persistently high-ethylene, near-zero-acetylene T3 signature can be produced by a shared/diffusing OLTC compartment rather than a genuine winding/core hot spot. If the OLTC compartment is clean, follow up with an electrical/frequency-response test to locate a circulating-current or connection hot spot.
